deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). X is a space stratified by a poset I. X_i is the closed union of strata, \dot X_i = ∪_{k<i} X_k, and X_i^* = X_i \ \dot X_i is the open stratum. For i ≤ j, V_ij is a (regular) neighbourhood of X_i^* inside X_j, with closure \overline V_ij, boundary \dot V_ij and 'âme' (core) X_i^* = V_ij ∩ X_i. V_ij^* = V_ij ∩ X_j^* is the deleted neighbourhood. The proposed 'pierres' (building blocks) are the diagrams X_j^* ← V_ij^* → V_ij → X_i^* (the last map being a retraction onto the core), with X_i^* recovered as the case i = j.

This page. Grothendieck immediately criticises these blocks. As they stand they are 'cotes mal taillées' (badly cut compromises). They are too general in one sense and not fine enough in another to capture the deleted neighbourhoods \dot V^{d'_*}_{d_*,d''_*} ≅ Ñ_{d_*;(d'_0,d''_0)} | D^*_{d_*} of his other manuscript 'Str_∞', p. 84.

He proposes smaller pieces, those V_ij^* with j a successor of i (j covers i in I: no k with i < k < j). Under standard hypotheses of smoothness and normal local triviality ('équisingularité'), which he says certainly hold for complex algebraic varieties stratified by closed subvarieties (i.e. Whitney/Thom–Mather conditions), he claims:
- V_ij^* is homeomorphic to a fibre bundle over the manifold X_i^* with fibre the open cylinder ℝ × C_ij, where C_ij is a compact manifold (the link of X_i^* in X_j).
- Correspondingly V_ij is a bundle of open cones on C_ij over X_i^*.
- When j is not a successor of i, C_ij is still a manifold but no longer compact.

The reason is that only strata k with i ≤ k ≤ j meet a small neighbourhood of X_i^* in X_j. If j covers i, the link lies entirely in X_j^* and is therefore a compact manifold. Otherwise its intersection with X_j^* is the open top stratum of a compact stratified link, hence a non-compact manifold.

Marginal note: the actual drawing gives a situation that is 'not nice but reasonable' yet fails the standard local-triviality type. The stratum shown should be replaced by two strata, i.e. the stratification should be refined.

The next page generalises the blocks to V^j_{i,k} for chains i ≤ j ≤ k, interpolating between V^*_{ik} and V_{ik}. He also already allows equivalence only 'up to homotopy or a weakened homeomorphism'.

Purpose: this is the 'dévissage' of tame stratified spaces into a diagram of ordinary manifolds (strata, link bundles, cylinders) and fibrations. It is the programme of Esquisse d'un programme §5–6, aimed at an algebraic/combinatorial description of stratified homotopy types.
errors: The phrase 'one can get by with smaller pieces' corresponding only to covering pairs (i, j) is too optimistic if read literally. Reconstructing X requires compatibility data along chains/flags i < j < k (corner structure), not just covering pairs. Grothendieck himself moves to chain-indexed pieces V^j_{i,k} on the next page.

'Homeomorphic to a fibre bundle' over X_i^* holds under Thom–Mather/Siebenmann-type hypotheses. The fibre C_ij may be empty or disconnected, and the global bundle structure needs control data, not just local triviality. This is minor and implicitly assumed.

ideas.what: Deleted regular neighbourhood of a stratum in a higher stratum is a bundle over the stratum with fibre ℝ × link; the full neighbourhood is a bundle of open cones on the link
ideas.modern_name: Link bundle / mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods (Thom–Mather control data; locally cone-like stratified sets)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (tame topology, dévissage of stratified structures), informally

ideas.what: For a covering pair i ⋖ j the link of X_i^* in X_j is a compact manifold; for non-covering pairs, the link's top part is a non-compact manifold
ideas.modern_name: Links of adjacent strata in a Whitney/conically smooth stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard folklore in stratification theory (Goresky–MacPherson, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 'unzipping')

ideas.what: Reconstructing a stratified space from building blocks (strata, link bundles, neighbourhoods) indexed by the stratification poset or its chains
ideas.modern_name: Dévissage / unzipping / resolution into manifolds with fibred corners; exit-path / stratified homotopy hypothesis
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984), Verona, Albin–Melrose, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2014–17), Lurie (HA App. A)

ideas.what: Need to refine a stratification (replace one stratum by two) so that standard equisingularity/local triviality holds

missed.claim: Working evidence of Grothendieck's unpublished manuscript 'Str_∞'. It contains at least 84 pages with explicit normal-neighbourhood objects Ñ_{d_*;(d'_0,d''_0)} | D^*_{d_*} indexed by flag data. This is a more detailed form of the dévissage only sketched in the Esquisse.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It points archivists and historians to a substantial companion text on stratified spaces. That text may anticipate the chain-indexed corner structures used by Albin–Melrose and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard Thom–Mather link-bundle structure plus the observation about covering pairs and compact links. Its role in the tame-topology dévissage is already announced in the Esquisse. The only item of interest is the cross-reference to the 'Str_∞' manuscript.
transcription_corrections: 'ces fameuses pièces telles qu'elles se sont citées mal faillies' should read approximately 'ces fameuses pierres telles quelles sont des cotes mal taillées'. The word is 'pierres', as on the previous page, not 'pièces'.
'pas assez [?] ... pour contenir' is probably 'pas assez fins pour contenir les voisinages'.
'Ces pièces sont particulières' should be 'Ces pierres sont particulièrement ...' (with a crossed-out word).
The 'stratifiées' inserted before 'par des sous-variétés alg. complexes fermées' is plausible.
'dessin [?] V^*_{i,j}' is likely an interlinear insertion ('i.e.' or similar) rather than 'dessin'.

Margin: 'Mais ce dessin (dans le dessin réel) donne une situation pas belle, mais raisonnable — qui ne pourrait pas avoir "type standard convenable" ...; le strat. X_i —•— devrait être remplacé par deux ...'.
